messages:
Oncall Bot: [ALERT] High error rate detected for enterprise customer Nebula Financial on dedicated pool nebula-prod-eu1 (eu-west-1). 5xx spike ~15% above baseline over the last 3m. Pager triggered. Incident ID INC-2025-1755.

Sophia Patel: I'm oncall today — grabbing this. @Miguel please join, looks like dedicated routing.

Miguel Alvarez: I'm on. quick look: grpc-proxy -> model-backend-1 returning lots of 504/503. p95 latency for backend up to 2.2s. pulling proxy logs now.

Priya Rao: Noted. I'll check autoscaler + kv cache pressure. If cache evictions are high we'll see token regen spikes.

Sophia Patel: Triage plan: 1) Confirm customer impact & scope 2) Try scale-up of dedicated pool 3) Toggle routing to fallback model-quant variant if scaling doesn't restore 4) Draft status page + customer notify.

Miguel Alvarez: Confirmed scope: only Nebula Financial dedicated pool in eu-west-1. No host-wide alerts. Metrics: request rate unchanged, error rate up only for that tenant.

Statusbot: DRAFT status: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting Nebula Financial's dedicated inference instance in eu-west-1. API calls to that dedicated pool may return errors or high latency. Our engineers are actively investigating and we will provide updates here. Incident ID INC-2025-1755."

Ashley Chen: CS prepping customer message. Need an account contact list + recommended customer mitigations (retry/backoff). Also confirm whether Nebula's production traffic is being routed to the fallback pool.

Eve (CS): Nebula contacts (from account): Jordan King (AM) jordan.king@nebula.com, +1-555-0123; Lila Park (DevOps) lila.park@nebula.com, +44-20-555-0199; Security contact: security@nebula.com. Legal looped in.

Sophia Patel: Thanks. Jordan, do you want a short proactive note to be sent now? We should be transparent: "We are investigating errors and working to restore service. We'll share a status page link and ETA."

Jordan King: Yes please — send them the short note and let them know we may enable fallback routing. They prefer phone for major incidents.

Priya Rao: Attempting mitigation: scaling dedicated pool now. Command:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-nebula-prod scale deployment/nebula-runtime --replicas=6
```
Also toggling cache retention to aggressive to reduce KV evictions: `NEBULA_CACHE_TTL=60s` (applied to configmap).

Deploy Bot: rollout/nebula-runtime scaled from 4 to 6 replicas (start). See rollout: https://k8s.company.internal/rollouts/nebula-runtime

Miguel Alvarez: While scaling is in progress, I'm tailing envoy logs. Seeing repeated `upstream connection reset by peer` from model-backend-1. Possibly connection limit at upstream or a memory pressure causing worker restarts.

Sophia Patel: If scaling doesn't reduce 5xx within 5-10m, plan B is to flip routing to quantized-compat model variant for Nebula pool to reduce backend load. That can be done via runtime config:
```
PATCH /v1/runtime/configs/nebula-prod -d '{"model_variant":"quant-compat","routing":{"prefer_local":true}}'
```
Will coordinate rollback after.

Ashley Chen: Draft customer template (short): 
"Hi Jordan — we're investigating elevated errors affecting your dedicated inference instance in eu-west-1. Our engineers are working on scale and routing mitigations. You may see transient 5xx responses or increased latency. We will update you within 15 minutes. If you'd like live updates via phone, reply here or call +1-555-0123 (oncall)."

Eve (CS): I'll send that and mark as high-touch. Also ask them to avoid large-batch requests until we stabilize.

Statusbot: Public status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/INC-2025-1755 — "Investigating: Elevated errors impacting Nebula Financial dedicated pool in eu-west-1."

Sophia Patel: Update: scaled replicas are coming up. Backend restart loop observed on backend-1 — likely an Envoy connection limit misconfiguration. Miguel is capturing pid logs and heap profiles.

Miguel Alvarez: Captured stack traces and heap info. Looks like the model process is hitting file descriptor limits, threads aborting, then envoy gets 5xx. Raising FD limits as immediate hotfix. Running: `sysctl -w fs.nr_open=1000000` then updating systemd unit with `LimitNOFILE=200000`.

Deploy Bot: Applying systemd unit change to nodes in nebula pool (rolling).

Priya Rao: After FD bump, error rate dropped from 15% -> 4% in the last 3m. Latency p95 reduced to ~800ms. Still above baseline but improving.

Sophia Patel: Good. Send customer update: "Mitigation in progress; we've applied resource limit increases and are scaling. Errors reduced but we're monitoring for full recovery. Next update in 30 minutes or when resolved."

Ashley Chen: Sent to Jordan (AM) + Lila (DevOps). Jordan confirmed receipt and requested an incident call if not resolved in 30m.

Jordan King: Thanks team. Please include a short RCA (impact, timeline, root cause) when available. They'll want to share internally.

Sophia Patel: Internal exec blurb (for product/ops): "Impact: Nebula Financial dedicated pool in eu-west-1 experienced elevated 5xx due to upstream FD/thread exhaustion on model backend. Scope: single enterprise customer dedicated pool. Mitigation: increased node FD limits and scaled runtime, optional routing to quantized model reduced load. Status: service restored to degraded -> recovering. Next: postmortem + overdue config hardening and automated FD checks."

Priya Rao: Please add follow-ups to post-incident action items: 1) automated FD monitoring & alerts 2) config drift check for systemd units in dedicated clusters 3) runbook update for Nebula dedicated pools (include fallback routing steps and contact matrix).

Statusbot: Follow-up status: "Monitoring: Errors decreased significantly following resource increase. We will keep the incident open for monitoring and conduct a full postmortem. Incident INC-2025-1755 — status: monitoring."

Sophia Patel: Final close message to customer drafted and approved: 
"Root cause: an OS-level file descriptor limit on model backend nodes caused worker failures and upstream errors. What we did: increased FD limits, scaled pool, applied temporary routing changes where needed. Impact: transient 5xx errors and elevated latency for requests to your dedicated pool in eu-west-1 between 15:12-15:52 UTC. Current status: service recovered and stabilized. Next steps: we will follow up with a full RCA and permanent remediation. Apologies for the disruption. — Redwood Inference SRE & CS"

Eve (CS): Sent final note to Nebula legal/ops + AMs. Jordan confirmed they are satisfied with the timeline and asked for the RCA within 48 hours.

Sophia Patel: Closing incident in 25m after monitoring window. Assigning postmortem owners: Miguel (root cause analysis), Priya (runbook + monitoring), Ashley (customer comms follow-up).

Deploy Bot: Incident INC-2025-1755 status changed -> monitoring -> resolved (pending postmortem).

Miguel Alvarez: Quick observation for RCA: config drift between our provisioning playbook and actual systemd units on edge nodes. Prioritize an automated reconciliation job.

Priya Rao: Adding the action items to ops backlog and creating the runbook PR now.

Sophia Patel: Thanks all. Great cross-team response. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
